item.content:encoded:
Resolution to Reaffirm Shared Governance in Instruction

We call for faculty to have the determinative role in instructional decisions, including those about curriculum, grading, and assessment. In accordance with the AAUP’s 1966 Statement on Government of Colleges and Universities, an essential principle of shared governance is that “when it comes to academic matters, a faculty decision should normally be the final decision” – faculty, not administrators, should set the curriculum and academic policy at the University of Michigan. Concerns raised by LSA faculty indicate that the recently announced first-semester grade-covering pilot did not receive sufficient faculty consultation before it was launched. We are also deeply concerned by President Grasso’s directive to LSA leadership to “pause” the program. It is for LSA faculty, not the President of the University, to determine how, on what terms, and in what manner grades are given to LSA students. We urge the U-M administration and LSA leadership to respect faculty authority and work with LSA faculty through a meaningful governance process for grade covering and any future instructional policies.   Approved by the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs (SACUA) on October 9, 2026. (PDF)

item.content:encoded: Recently, some members of the University of Michigan community have been visited at night by anonymous groups who reportedly banged on doors, shined lights through windows, made loud noises, and otherwise sought to intimidate residents who were believed to be associated with the UM-LANL computing center (the groups were heard to chant “Stop the datacenter!”). UM community members express a broad range of views about the center, but whatever the underlying concerns, the targeting of individuals with threatening and abusive behavior is inimical to democracy and academic values. As representatives of the Faculty Senate, SACUA supports freedom of expression and peaceful protest, but categorically condemns violence, threats, intimidation, doxxing, and harassment. As a practical matter, research suggests that the latter can be counterproductive even for the goals of persuasion or protest. The identities of the perpetrators are unknown at this time, and we make no assumptions about them. Meanwhile, SACUA urges all members of the university community to re-commit to and uphold peaceful means of expression, debate, and protest. To the extent we have differences, they should be addressed through deliberation and nonviolent action. Approved by the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs (SACUA) on September 9, 2026 PDF of Statement

item.content:encoded:
Statement Congratulating President-Elect C. Cybele Raver as 17th President

On behalf of the faculty of the University of Michigan, the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs (SACUA) congratulates Dr. C. Cybele Raver on her selection as our 17th president and welcomes her to the UM community. Dr. Raver's experience and accomplishments, both as a scholar and as an administrator, are impressive and serve as excellent background for the role. As a professor of psychology, she conducted groundbreaking research with real-world impact on early childhood education, with a focus on social-emotional development of children from lower-income families. Dr. Raver has also served as Vice Provost at New York University, and most recently as Vice Chancellor and Provost at Vanderbilt University, where she oversaw significant growth in the university’s research activity. We thank our Regents for overseeing the presidential search process and for selecting a leader with an exceptional record both as an academic and university administrator. We also thank the members of the Presidential Search Advisory Committee for their time, effort, and diligence in evaluating candidates. Dr. Raver, we look forward to welcoming you in the coming months. We are encouraged by your commitment to working alongside our faculty, staff, students, and alumni, and are eager to collaborate with you in advancing the university’s collective mission.   Approved by the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs on August 19, 2026. item.title: Faculty Senate Chair Newsletter – 07/01/2026
item.author: Meaghan Blanchard
item.description:
Dear Faculty Senate Members,
I hope your summer days are unfolding as planned! Here is a slightly late June newsletter:
OMB Rule on Federal Grants: A proposed rule would make federal grants contingent on political approval, not only scholarly merit. VP of Research, Skip Lupia, and others are coordinating a university response. You can also respond individually, as indicated below.
Introducing Vice Chair Kirsten Herold: Kirsten, from the School of Public Health, is the first Lecturer to serve on SACUA, and this year’s Faculty Senate Vice Chair.
New AI Committee: The potential impacts of AI are varied, and opinions about it are diverse. To consider issues most relevant to the university, SACUA is forming an AI committee. Help determine its charge by answering just one multiple-response question in this survey.
Results from Last Month’s Survey: Respondents expressed broad satisfaction with their colleagues, students, and university resources. Other responses pointed to eroding shared governance at the university and ideological tensions among the faculty.
Statement regarding Regent Acker: An investigation confirmed previous allegations of vulgar comments by Regent Acker. SACUA is calling on him to resign.

item.title: Statement Concerning Regent Acker
item.author: Eric Vandenberghe
item.description: Now that a formal investigation and Regent Jordan Acker’s own remarks have verified earlier allegations of obscene comments he made about an undergraduate UM student, among others, we call on him to resign from the Board of the University of Michigan. The statement Mr. Acker delivered at the Regents meeting on June 25, 2026, was neither a genuine apology nor accountability, and we do not accept any claim that it was either. A true apology would have specified what he was apologizing for and indicated to whom he was making the apology. Accountability would have involved some form of atonement, as […]
item.content:encoded: Now that a formal investigation and Regent Jordan Acker’s own remarks have verified earlier allegations of obscene comments he made about an undergraduate UM student, among others, we call on him to resign from the Board of the University of Michigan. The statement Mr. Acker delivered at the Regents meeting on June 25, 2026, was neither a genuine apology nor accountability, and we do not accept any claim that it was either. A true apology would have specified what he was apologizing for and indicated to whom he was making the apology. Accountability would have involved some form of atonement, as well as recognition that it does not help the university to have a leader confirmed to have made such comments. He could have resigned; reimbursed UM for the significant costs of what could have been an unnecessary investigation; assigned himself relevant community service; or perhaps all of the above. Continuing on the Board as if nothing has happened is not accountability. It demonstrates that his judgment has not improved since the reported events, and that, in turn, suggests he is unfit to influence such important decisions as selecting UM’s next president. As faculty who share in the governance of this university, we feel ashamed. And, as no true apology appears forthcoming from Mr. Acker, we apologize both to the victims of his remarks for his aspersive, derogatory, and deeply invasive comments and to the broader University of Michigan community for his failure to model our values. Approved by the Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs (SACUA) on July 1, 2026. PDF of statement
